title: Where Niagara Residents Can Set Off Fireworks for Diwali, City by City
excerpt: Niagara Falls permits Diwali fireworks November 7-11 and St. Catharines November 7-9, each with strict hours and private-property rules. Welland's bylaw does not list Diwali, and Thorold requires the Fire Chief's written approval for other holidays.
body:
• Niagara Falls permits consumer fireworks for Diwali: on the day, the day before and three days after — Sunday, November 8, plus November 7 and November 9-11, 2026 — between 6 p.m. and 11 p.m., on private property only.
  • St. Catharines permits consumer fireworks on Diwali and the day immediately before and after — November 7, 8 and 9 — between dusk and 11 p.m., on your own land or private land with the owner's permission, for adults 18 and over.
  • Welland's published fireworks bylaw announcement lists only Victoria Day and Canada Day, plus the three days preceding each — Diwali is not a permitted day there as of right.
  • Thorold allows fireworks as of right only around Victoria Day and Canada Day; other celebratory holidays, including a Diwali display, need the Fire Chief's prior written approval.

Diwali falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026, and whether you can legally set off fireworks at home for it in Ontario's Niagara region depends entirely on which municipality you live in. Niagara Falls and St. Catharines both name Diwali in their fireworks rules. Welland and Thorold do not give Diwali the same standing. Here is what each city's own bylaw material says.

Niagara Falls: yes, November 7-11, 6 to 11 p.m.

The City of Niagara Falls lists Diwali among the holidays recognized in its fireworks by-law, alongside Chinese New Year, Victoria Day and Canada Day. Under the city's Fireworks and Pyrotechnics page, fireworks may be set off only on an approved holiday, the day before it, and three days after it, and only between 6 p.m. and 11 p.m. For Diwali 2026, that window is Saturday, November 7, through Wednesday, November 11.

In its Diwali reminder to residents, the city adds the conditions: fireworks may be discharged only on private property with the property owner's permission, and are prohibited in or over public spaces including parks, streets, sidewalks and public parking lots. You must be at least 18 to purchase or discharge consumer fireworks. Fireworks must not be discharged when wind speeds exceed 20 km/h or when a fire ban is in effect, and they must be kept clear of buildings, vehicles, overhead wires and neighbouring properties. A permit is required to sell fireworks or host a public display, and fireworks may be sold only during designated periods, including the seven days preceding Diwali.

"Our primary goal is ensuring everyone can celebrate safely, and that starts with keeping fireworks out of our shared public areas."

— A.J. Lunn, Public Education Officer, Niagara Falls Fire Department

St. Catharines: yes, November 7-9, dusk to 11 p.m.

St. Catharines updated its fireworks by-law in 2022 specifically to recognize the city's growing diversity and permit consumer fireworks during Diwali, according to the Fire Services report that brought the replacement by-law to council. The by-law text published with that report allows consumer fireworks to be discharged only on Victoria Day, Canada Day and Diwali, and on the day immediately preceding and the day immediately following each. For Diwali 2026, that is November 7, 8 and 9.

The conditions are narrower than in Niagara Falls. Discharge is allowed only between dusk and 11 p.m., unless the Fire Chief gives written permission otherwise. No one under 18 may discharge consumer fireworks. An adult may discharge them on land belonging to them, or on other privately owned land where the owner has given permission. Fireworks may not be discharged in or on a highway, street, lane, square, parkland or other public place without the Fire Chief's prior written permission, and sky lanterns are prohibited outright.

Welland: Diwali is not a permitted day

Welland is different. The city's published announcement for Fireworks Bylaw 2003-127 states that fireworks are only permitted on Victoria Day and Canada Day, as well as the three days preceding Victoria Day and Canada Day. Diwali is not in that list, so a home Diwali display in Welland is not permitted as of right under the bylaw material the city publishes. The announcement also reminds residents that fireworks are not to be ignited on public property, including parks and open fields, and that contraventions can bring a fine of up to $5,000.

Thorold: approval first for other holidays

Thorold's Fireworks By-Law 37-2024 allows consumer fireworks as of right only around Victoria Day and Canada Day — the two days immediately preceding, the day itself, and the two days immediately following each. Any other celebratory holiday requires prior written approval from the Fire Chief. Where fireworks are permitted, Thorold's window is 6 p.m. to 11 p.m.; fireworks may not be discharged from, onto or over a highway, street, sidewalk, park or other public place, over utility lines, or in wind speeds above 20 km/h, and not during a fire ban.

What to do before you light anything

Check your own municipality first, using the links above — in Niagara, the answer changes across a city line. If your city is not covered here, or your plan falls outside the permitted days and hours, contact your local fire department before Diwali weekend rather than assuming a neighbour city's rule applies to you. The permitted windows above are for consumer fireworks on private property; public displays and sales are separately regulated in every municipality listed.
